title: PRD: Cohort-driven evaluation harness, graduated A/B gates, and staged failover for Optimize
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This PRD defines a production-ready evaluation harness for Optimize that: (1) uses cohort-driven and sentinel prompt sampling; (2) gates A/B rollouts with statistical and business thresholds; and (3) implements a graded rollback/failover policy that escalates from automated throttles to full traffic rollback. The goal is to reduce undetected regressions while keeping rollout velocity high for model and configuration updates.
background: We have recurring incidents where model/config rollouts pass coarse checks but produce regression in specific customer cohorts or long-tail prompts. Current canaries are per-model and global; they miss cohort-specific quality regressions and provide coarse binary pass/fail decisions. Optimize needs a more granular, actionable evaluation contract that ties observable signals to deterministic remediation steps and human-in-the-loop triage when necessary.
goals: Detect cohort-specific degradation with >90% recall for regressions causing >5% business-impact metric change
Prevent silent regressions by introducing sentinel prompt detection and progressive gating across traffic slices
Define deterministic rollback/playbook actions that reduce mean time to mitigation (MTTM) to under 20 minutes for high-severity regressions
Enable safe rapid rollouts: initial canary to 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with objective pass criteria at each stage
non_goals: Improve underlying model training processes (this is a serving/eval policy change, not an ML re-training initiative)
Replace manual post-deploy human QA for complex policy/regulatory cases
Provide full auto-rollback for noisy low-signal metrics without human review
requirements: Create a library of sentinel prompts organized by cohort (customer persona, region, latency-sensitive flows, regulatory flows)
Define cohort definitions and labeling rules so traffic is deterministically bucketed at request time
Implement an evaluation pipeline that computes per-cohort metrics in near-real-time (max 5 minute lag)
Provide configurable A/B gate rules in Console for: min sample size, minimum detectable effect, alpha, beta, and max allowed regression
Ship a staged rollback engine that can: gradually throttle traffic, divert to previous model version, or full rollback; each action tied to clear trigger conditions
Integrate HIL (human-in-the-loop) notification and approval steps for ambiguous signals
Expose evaluation results and runbook links in per-release Console UI and in Slack/PagerDuty alerts
acceptance_criteria: Sentinel library with >= 500 prompts covering at least 8 predefined cohorts exists and is versioned in Optimize
Per-cohort metrics (accuracy proxy, hallucination rate, latency P95, token cost) are computed and stored with <=5 minute latency
A/B gate config supports: alpha=0.05, beta=0.2 defaults and allows override per-release
Minimum sample size calculator included in UI and enforced for gating decisions

Automated rollback triggers implemented: (a) immediate throttle if a safety sentinel > 0.5% absolute regression, (b) automatic 50% traffic revert if composite quality score drops >3% sustained for 10 minutes, (c) full rollback if business KPI regression >5% for 5 minutes
Playbook linked in Console for each trigger with owner, checklist, and communication templates
End-to-end test harness that simulates cohorts and verifies gating/rollback behavior in staging
rollout_strategy: Phase 0: Staging validation with synthetic traffic (2 weeks) -> Phase 1: Internal canary (1%) for 48 hours -> Phase 2: Beta customers (5%) for 72 hours -> Phase 3: Gradual ramp (20% for 24 hours, 100% if gates pass). Each phase requires passing cohort-specific gates. If any cohort fails a gate, automated action is applied per remediation_playbook and the release is paused pending investigation.
statistical_tests: Default statistical test: two-sided proportion test for binary signals (e.g., sentinel hit rate) and t-test (Welch) for continuous scores (e.g., quality score). Default alpha=0.05. Enforce minimum detectable effect calculation in UI: MDE = z_{1-alpha/2}*sqrt(p*(1-p)*(1/n1+1/n2)). Minimum n computed and must be met for the gate to be valid. For low-signal cohorts use sequential analysis with alpha spending (e.g., Pocock boundary) to allow earlier decisions while controlling Type I error.
remediation_playbook: Level 1 (Transient noise): Auto-throttle new release traffic by 50% and notify on-call; retry observations for 15 minutes
Level 2 (Cohort regression): Divert failed cohort traffic to previous stable variant, create high-priority investigation ticket, and open a dedicated War Room channel
Level 3 (Business KPI impact): Immediate full rollback of the release, notify customers via status page and account reps, schedule postmortem within 48 hours
Human-in-the-loop: For signals classified as ambiguous by the composite detector, create a Hold state pending reviewer approval; reviewers have 30 minutes SLO to act for P1 releases
monitoring_signals: Composite quality score per cohort (weighted accuracy + hallucination penalty + latency penalty)
Business KPIs: conversion rate, retention signal (as provided by customer integrations)
Infrastructure signals: token cost variance, GPU latency P95, request error rate
Anomaly detectors: drift in distribution (embedding distance) and abrupt change in output length
ui_changes: Console: Release details page gains a Cohort tab (per-cohort metrics, sentinel breakdown, sample viewer) and a Gates panel showing pass/fail status and confidence intervals. Gate configuration page allows setting alpha/beta, MDE, and remediation actions. Notifications configuration for slack/PagerDuty integrated into release flow.
data_and_infra: Storage for per-request metadata and evaluation events (retention 90 days)
Streaming pipeline (Kafka) to route sampled requests to evaluation workers
Evaluation workers to run controlled prompts and compute metrics; need autoscaling profile and quotas
Dashboard endpoints and Console API to surface near-real-time cohort results
open_questions: What is acceptable latency tradeoff for running sentinel prompts synchronously vs async?
Which cohorts should be 'blocked cohorts' (always require human approval) for the first release? Suggested: top-10 enterprise customers + EU-regulated flows
Who is the escalation owner after hours for Level 2 cohort regressions?
Should we surface raw model outputs in Console for sampled requests or only aggregated signals? Compliance implications
